approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs using only the current task's accepted scores. It chooses parents from high-scoring population quantiles, builds a surplus pool through connected-fragment crossover or local atom/bond mutations, and keeps a bounded population of the best observed molecules. Ordinary single-parent proposals sample one, two or three successive mutation calls; prolonged unsuccessful pool filling can raise that floor. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Stable canonical identities and duplicate rejection govern admission. A Gaussian posterior over integer-count Morgan fingerprints, using generalized Tanimoto similarity, learns from the full accepted archive. Correlated posterior score draws then select distinct pool members for each announced batch.
approach.novelty: This control removes optional ordinary mutation continuation: when the saturation floor is one, the first mutation-call result proceeds to the existing admission and selection path without a second or third call. The original length draw remains, and higher-floor recovery, internal mutation retries and crossover finishing mutation remain intact. Earlier siblings removed crossover, sampled residual influence, residual correlation or fingerprint multiplicity. This experiment instead isolates ordinary continuation on their shared exchange-free Parent. A historical continuation removal lost endpoint score on an exchange-enabled composition; the new test asks whether the retained route still contributes here. The predicted loss concerns endpoint search, even if first-product acceptance or local parent-beating yield improves.

hypothesis: Remove optional second and third successive GraphOperators.mutate calls from ordinary single-parent proposals when the inherited saturation floor is one, retaining the original sampled base-length draw and the full max(base length, saturation floor) schedule whenever that floor exceeds one.

finding_summary.headline: Ordinary continuation contributes to endpoint search: its removal lowers all three seed macros.
finding_summary.insights:
The removal exposed useful first products, yet useful local steps did not preserve final search quality. Across the whole Child, parent beats increased from 629 to 714 and incumbent improvements from 258 to 299 while endpoints fell. Those counts depend on changing ancestors and incumbents; they cannot tell us what the omitted continuations would have scored. This resolves the previously open current-composition contribution question, separately from the earlier exchange-enabled experiment. It does not make the separate crossover and posterior-component losses additive.

The molecular assessment helps narrow the next question to coverage of useful structural arrangements. The Child still finds varied aromatic, carbonyl and amine families, but its leading repeated aza-aryl family does not recover the Parent’s compact carbonyl-thione organization. Some other families improve, and reactive bonds, difficult ring geometries and unspecified stereochemistry persist on both sides. Fewer calls therefore do not establish chemically simpler or more feasible output. These associations do not identify which omitted product or molecular feature caused the score loss. Saturation recovery remains untested, and fewer calls did not yield an observed speedup: total wall time was about 1,778 seconds versus 579, alongside much greater oracle time on the changed molecules.
finding_summary.results:
Ordinary second and third mutation calls disappeared under real requests for longer walks. The Child made one call in all 41,665 ordinary attempts; 7,373 requests would have allowed continuation, suppressing 8,589 requested calls. The Parent actually executed 8,737 continuation calls. Of the affected first-call products, 6,980 entered the candidate pools and 518 reached accepted evaluation; 100 beat their generating parent and 35 improved the incumbent. Internal retries, crossover finishing mutations and correlated posterior selection remained active. Neither side exercised saturation recovery.

The complete matched three-seed panel fell from mean final Top-1 0.595670 to 0.568802, a paired change of -0.026868, exceeding the registered 0.002 loss scale. Seed changes were -0.047714, -0.009154 and -0.023735. Population dispersion decreased from 0.026593 to 0.012088, but every seed macro was lower. Ten task-seed endpoints declined and five improved: all three median_2 endpoints, zaleplon_mpo in seed zero, and sitagliptin_mpo in seed one. Three task means declined and two rose. Correct execution and the predicted endpoint loss support a positive contribution from retained ordinary continuation in this composition.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families persist, with enlarged repeats, unusual N-halogen bonds, strained rings and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: For n-dbee08307e86, all supplied Child and published Parent n-62daf219c70a trajectory paths were present and read. The brief independently reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, matched Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, and no profile-mismatched seeds. No task is omitted and no comparison path is missing. Each task supplies 900 Child records, including 870 optimizer records; the Parent panel is also complete. The paired files share their fixed initial molecules and scores. The digest final_molecules are late seed-2 proposals, not the retained best molecule for every seed; the full trajectories determine the per-seed descriptions below. Output includes compact aromatic ketones and amides, very large repeated aza-aryl ethers, linked carbonyl-rich heterocycles, flexible and cyclic polyamines, fused or bridged nitrogen-carbonyl systems, and fluorinated imino heterocycles. Child ring-closure-string incidences are 0.9713, 0.9782, 0.9839, 0.9839 and 0.9644 in the fixed task order; aromatic-string incidences are 0.9701, 0.9782, 0.9828, 0.9782 and 0.908. These are incidences of SMILES text features, not ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 throughout, although available aliphatic amines and potentially stereogenic saturated centres occur. Size and ring descriptions were checked with the locked RDKit environment directly on these trajectory graphs; this does not establish synthesis, conformation, stability or biological activity. Ring and aromatic content are rich. Structural diversity is moderate across tasks and seeds, but leaders within a seed commonly share a scaffold. Drug-likeness is weak overall because familiar medicinal functional groups coexist with N-halogen bonds, peroxides, repeated large assemblies and difficult small-ring or bridged geometries. The Parent already exhibited these general concerns: its full report and the original n-c55c3d520a2c molecular report were read through the evidence index. Their historical origin is retained in each transferable gap; older-profile evidence is not another current replica. The current Child changes the realized chemical families, including a much larger repeated aza-aromatic family and a fluorinated leader without the Parent leader's cyclic cumulene. It does not establish uniform chemical improvement or loss. All literal molecular citations below are Child molecules allowed by the digest or trusted citation_trajectory_paths; Parent-only structures are identified descriptively by task/seed/evaluation in the published trajectories. Chemistry associations here do not identify activation, attribute a liability to ordinary continuation, assign scores to omitted products, or isolate a mediator of the paired endpoint contrast. The audit is .slots/r0016-02-ablation-L01/molecular/trajectory_audit.json; inspected_records.json retains every read graph, score, source path and descriptive calculation.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 leader (evaluation 296) is a compact aza-indole-like fused aromatic system attached through an alpha-fluorinated ketone to pyridine; it carries vinyl, methyl and ethyl groups and fluorine on the fused-ring nitrogen. Seed 0 instead retains an indole/azaaryl amide with an additional fused saturated four-membered carbocycle, methoxy and fluoromethyl substituents, and an N-chloro or N-fluoro amide. Seed 2 reaches a benzene-fused unsaturated four-membered carbocycle bearing vinyl ether, methylamino and alpha-bromo ketone substituents. Thus most leading material is compact, aromatic and carbonyl-containing, not deficient in rings or heteroatoms. Mean Child SMILES length is 42.4 and halogen-string incidence is 0.8667. The Parent seed-0 leader (evaluation 289) instead contains an amino-substituted cumulene; its seed-1 leader (293) is an N-hydroxy pyridyl amide and its seed-2 leader (294) a vicinal diketone. The Child seed-0 endpoint is higher, while the other matched seeds are lower. Both panels retain questionable local chemistry on recognizable aromatic frameworks.
liabilities: N-F on the fused heterocycle and N-Cl/N-F on an amide are distinct from conventional aromatic C-F/C-Cl substitutions and raise environment-specific stability and synthesis concerns.

The alpha-halo ketones are potentially electrophilic, while the seed-2 unsaturated four-membered fused carbocycle raises a geometric concern. A saturated fused four-membered ring is a different case and is not rejected merely for its size.
Vinyl ether, N-N-containing nearby variants and unassigned saturated centres complicate the chemical interpretation of otherwise familiar aromatic molecules.
missing_features: High-scoring, conventional local substitutions preserving the favorable aromatic/carbonyl organization are not consistently demonstrated; ordinary N-H indole amide chemistry is present initially, so this is a reliability gap rather than an inability to produce an amide.
Explicit stereochemical identity is absent for the alpha-halo ketone centres, and the small unsaturated fused-ring arrangement lacks demonstrated accessible geometry.
The available gradient does not identify an exact absent target pharmacophore or support simply increasing rings, donors or halogens.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This concern originates in n-c55c3d520a2c and was carried by n-62daf219c70a. It is re-observed here in n-dbee08307e86 against that published Parent on the complete matched Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 observations per objective, batch size 10 and the frozen Research-in-Depth epoch-1 profile with direct aromatic exchange disabled. Historical origin is not additional replication. Current leaders include N-F on aromatic or amide nitrogens, N-Cl amides, alpha-halo ketones, peroxides, an aziridine/aminal arrangement and unusual S=C/S=O substitution. Counterexamples matter: a conventional ethoxy analogue closely approaches its peroxide relative, a high-scoring flexible aryl tertiary amine avoids N-halogen bonds, and a leading fluorinated family in one seed uses only carbon-bound fluorine. These are selective bond-environment concerns, not absence of amines, heterocycles or ordinary halogen chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently retain conventional local bond environments while preserving useful aromatic, carbonyl and amine relationships.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide bond-environment-aware transformations and plausible local alternatives that preserve favorable relationships learned from the current task's feedback. Distinguish carbon-bound halogens and ordinary amine centres from reactive heteroatom-halogen or highly strained arrangements. No blanket halogen, nitrogen, peroxide or small-ring ban, guaranteed score gain, or attribution to a particular retained or removed component follows from this association.

This motivates evaluating feasibility, not prohibiting ring formation or treating lower apparent strain as an established endpoint benefit; the observed topology change does not isolate a molecular mediator.

The finding is uneven leading-family coverage, not universal collapse, inability to create rings or evidence that the Child chemistry is uniformly worse.

This conditional coverage gap does not establish that any specific search component caused convergence, that a missing Parent molecule was a suppressed product, or that more diversity necessarily improves the objective.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs using only the current task's accepted scores. It chooses parents from high-scoring population quantiles, builds a surplus pool through connected-fragment crossover or local atom/bond mutations, and keeps a bounded population of the best observed molecules. Ordinary single-parent proposals sample one, two or three successive mutation calls; prolonged unsuccessful pool filling can raise that floor. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Stable canonical identities and duplicate rejection govern admission. A Gaussian posterior over integer-count Morgan fingerprints, using generalized Tanimoto similarity, learns from the full accepted archive. Correlated posterior score draws then select distinct pool members for each announced batch.
approach.novelty: This control removes optional ordinary mutation continuation: when the saturation floor is one, the first mutation-call result proceeds to the existing admission and selection path without a second or third call. The original length draw remains, and higher-floor recovery, internal mutation retries and crossover finishing mutation remain intact. Earlier siblings removed crossover, sampled residual influence, residual correlation or fingerprint multiplicity. This experiment instead isolates ordinary continuation on their shared exchange-free Parent. A historical continuation removal lost endpoint score on an exchange-enabled composition; the new test asks whether the retained route still contributes here. The predicted loss concerns endpoint search, even if first-product acceptance or local parent-beating yield improves.

finding_summary.headline: Ordinary continuation contributes to endpoint search: its removal lowers all three seed macros.
finding_summary.insights:
The removal exposed useful first products, yet useful local steps did not preserve final search quality. Across the whole Child, parent beats increased from 629 to 714 and incumbent improvements from 258 to 299 while endpoints fell. Those counts depend on changing ancestors and incumbents; they cannot tell us what the omitted continuations would have scored. This resolves the previously open current-composition contribution question, separately from the earlier exchange-enabled experiment. It does not make the separate crossover and posterior-component losses additive.

The molecular assessment helps narrow the next question to coverage of useful structural arrangements. The Child still finds varied aromatic, carbonyl and amine families, but its leading repeated aza-aryl family does not recover the Parent’s compact carbonyl-thione organization. Some other families improve, and reactive bonds, difficult ring geometries and unspecified stereochemistry persist on both sides. Fewer calls therefore do not establish chemically simpler or more feasible output. These associations do not identify which omitted product or molecular feature caused the score loss. Saturation recovery remains untested, and fewer calls did not yield an observed speedup: total wall time was about 1,778 seconds versus 579, alongside much greater oracle time on the changed molecules.
finding_summary.results:
Ordinary second and third mutation calls disappeared under real requests for longer walks. The Child made one call in all 41,665 ordinary attempts; 7,373 requests would have allowed continuation, suppressing 8,589 requested calls. The Parent actually executed 8,737 continuation calls. Of the affected first-call products, 6,980 entered the candidate pools and 518 reached accepted evaluation; 100 beat their generating parent and 35 improved the incumbent. Internal retries, crossover finishing mutations and correlated posterior selection remained active. Neither side exercised saturation recovery.

The complete matched three-seed panel fell from mean final Top-1 0.595670 to 0.568802, a paired change of -0.026868, exceeding the registered 0.002 loss scale. Seed changes were -0.047714, -0.009154 and -0.023735. Population dispersion decreased from 0.026593 to 0.012088, but every seed macro was lower. Ten task-seed endpoints declined and five improved: all three median_2 endpoints, zaleplon_mpo in seed zero, and sitagliptin_mpo in seed one. Three task means declined and two rose. Correct execution and the predicted endpoint loss support a positive contribution from retained ordinary continuation in this composition.

finding_summary.headline: Ordinary continuation contributes to endpoint search: its removal lowers all three seed macros.
finding_summary.insights:
The removal exposed useful first products, yet useful local steps did not preserve final search quality. Across the whole Child, parent beats increased from 629 to 714 and incumbent improvements from 258 to 299 while endpoints fell. Those counts depend on changing ancestors and incumbents; they cannot tell us what the omitted continuations would have scored. This resolves the previously open current-composition contribution question, separately from the earlier exchange-enabled experiment. It does not make the separate crossover and posterior-component losses additive.

The molecular assessment helps narrow the next question to coverage of useful structural arrangements. The Child still finds varied aromatic, carbonyl and amine families, but its leading repeated aza-aryl family does not recover the Parent’s compact carbonyl-thione organization. Some other families improve, and reactive bonds, difficult ring geometries and unspecified stereochemistry persist on both sides. Fewer calls therefore do not establish chemically simpler or more feasible output. These associations do not identify which omitted product or molecular feature caused the score loss. Saturation recovery remains untested, and fewer calls did not yield an observed speedup: total wall time was about 1,778 seconds versus 579, alongside much greater oracle time on the changed molecules.
finding_summary.results:
Ordinary second and third mutation calls disappeared under real requests for longer walks. The Child made one call in all 41,665 ordinary attempts; 7,373 requests would have allowed continuation, suppressing 8,589 requested calls. The Parent actually executed 8,737 continuation calls. Of the affected first-call products, 6,980 entered the candidate pools and 518 reached accepted evaluation; 100 beat their generating parent and 35 improved the incumbent. Internal retries, crossover finishing mutations and correlated posterior selection remained active. Neither side exercised saturation recovery.

The complete matched three-seed panel fell from mean final Top-1 0.595670 to 0.568802, a paired change of -0.026868, exceeding the registered 0.002 loss scale. Seed changes were -0.047714, -0.009154 and -0.023735. Population dispersion decreased from 0.026593 to 0.012088, but every seed macro was lower. Ten task-seed endpoints declined and five improved: all three median_2 endpoints, zaleplon_mpo in seed zero, and sitagliptin_mpo in seed one. Three task means declined and two rose. Correct execution and the predicted endpoint loss support a positive contribution from retained ordinary continuation in this composition.

Across the whole Child, parent beats increased from 629 to 714 and incumbent improvements from 258 to 299 while endpoints fell. Those counts depend on changing ancestors and incumbents; they cannot tell us what the omitted continuations would have scored. This resolves the previously open current-composition contribution question, separately from the earlier exchange-enabled experiment. The molecular assessment helps narrow the next question to coverage of useful structural arrangements. The Child still finds varied aromatic, carbonyl and amine families, but its leading repeated aza-aryl family does not recover the Parent’s compact carbonyl-thione organization. Some other families improve, and reactive bonds, difficult ring geometries and unspecified stereochemistry persist on both sides. Fewer calls therefore do not establish chemically simpler or more feasible output. These associations do not identify which omitted product or molecular feature caused the score loss.
